title: Depth reduction for depth-2 circuits over narrow gates
statement:
Let $c$ be a Boolean circuit of depth exactly $2$ on $m$ inputs, and let $g_1,\dots,g_m \colon \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ be Boolean functions such that each $g_i$ is computed both by a DNF formula of width at most $l$ and by a CNF formula of width at most $l$, where the width of a DNF or CNF formula is the maximum number of literals occurring in any single one of its terms or clauses. Then there exist a number $m'$, DNF formulas $D_1,\dots,D_{m'}$ on $n$ variables, and a Boolean circuit $c'$ of depth at most $1$ on $m'$ inputs, such that each $D_j$ has width at most $l$, every term of every $D_j$ contains each variable at most once (equivalently, its literals are pairwise distinct and no two of them share a variable), and for every assignment $x \in \{0,1\}^n$,
\[ c\bigl(g_1(x),\dots,g_m(x)\bigr) = c'\bigl(D_1(x),\dots,D_{m'}(x)\bigr). \]
hypotheses_covered: gate functions g_i on n-bit inputs
each g_i computed by a width-≤ l DNF
each g_i computed by a width-≤ l CNF
replaced:
A circuit $c$ of depth exactly $2$ over gates with width-$l$ DNF and CNF representations
reduces to a circuit $c'$ of depth at most $1$ over a fresh gate family $\mathrm{gates}'$
of width-$l$ DNFs (with duplicate-free, non-repeating-variable terms), so that $c$ and
$c'$ compute the same function on every $x$.
